Businesses today are  
in constant evolution.
Reimagining how they build, reducing impact while staying efficient. Designing 
experiences that feel seamless, personal and consistent at every touchpoint.
And extending care beyond boundaries, using data to deliver better 
outcomes, everywhere.
Different industries. Different journeys. 
Different priorities. Yet all are moving towards 
the same need to stay connected across systems, 
respond in real time, and make decisions with clarity.
In a world where technology is advancing at 
extraordinary speed, enterprises are navigating an 
ever-deepening layer of complexity legacy systems, 
fragmented data, expanding platforms, and rising 
expectations for seamless, omni-channel experiences. 
At the same time, the stakes are higher than ever, with 
growing demands for speed, resilience, security and 
trust. Managing this complexity while staying future-
ready is the defining reality of modern business.
This is where Tata Communications’ digital fabric 
comes in. It simplifies complexity by orchestrating 
cloud, edge, network and security into one cohesive, 
intelligent ecosystem.
More than connectivity, it enables transformation. 
By unifying disparate systems into an integrated 
architecture, it enhances visibility, simplifies 
management, and creates a secure, scalable 
foundation for hyperconnected operations that helps 
organisations move faster, innovate smarter, and 
operate with confidence.Together, limitlessTM
In today’s world, progress is no longer defined by what one 
company can achieve alone.
‘Together, limitlessTM’ is a statement of intent. It 
reflects Tata Communications’ belief that meaningful 
progress is unlocked through deep collaboration across 
customers, partners and teams, unbounded by geography, 
scale or convention.
Our relevance has grown alongside our customers’ 
ambitions. This promise reflects our ability to evolve at 
speed, shaping ourselves around our customers’ business 
outcomes, as they transform.
At its core, it defines how we show up, bringing together 
our platforms, expertise and people with our customers’ 
vision, and working side by side to overcome complexity 
with clarity and purpose. Because in a landscape 
often defined by noise, what enterprises seek most is 
integration, trust, and a partner who can help them move 
forward with confidence.
The next five years will shape the next fifty. As AI, cloud 
and edge converge in unprecedented ways, enterprises will 
need ecosystems that can adapt, scale and evolve in real 
time. Positioned at this intersection, Tata Communications 
is building for what comes next - where technologies align, 
innovation accelerates, and possibilities expand.
By enabling real-time, always-on, anywhere operations and 
unlocking the power of integrated data and intelligence, 
we help businesses move with clarity and confidence.
Because when systems work as one, complexity fades 
and when ambition is supported by the right foundation – 
possibilities become limitless.

About the Report Performance that Powers 
Possibilities
SDGsReporting Period 
This Report is published for the 12-month period from April 
1, 2025 to March 31, 2026. Where relevant, comparative 
data from earlier periods has been included to provide a 
contextual perspective.Our Approach
Integrated thinking shapes how we design strategy, allocate 
capital and measure performance. We prioritise matters that are 
material to our business and stakeholders, aligning them with 
long-term growth, risk management and responsible governance. 
By linking financial outcomes with environmental, social and 
operational performance, we ensure that decision-making 
remains disciplined, forward-looking and resilient in a rapidly 
evolving digital ecosystem.
Value creation through integrated thinking
Our approach shapes how we respond to:
	yMaterial matters impacting enterprise value
	yShort, medium and long-term performance priorities
	yCapital allocation and risk management
	ySustainability imperatives
Stakeholder engagement is embedded within the value creation 
process, ensuring that our use of and impact on the capitals 
remains balanced, accountable and aligned with long-term 
strategic objectives.

Reporting frameworks and principles
This Integrated Annual Report has been prepared in accordance 
with the guiding principles and content elements of the IIRC 
Framework. Disclosures within this Report are mapped, where 
applicable, to the Global Reporting Initiative (‘GRI’) Standards. 
The financial and statutory sections of the Report comply with 
the following: (a)The Companies Act, 2013, (b) Indian Accounting 
Standards (Ind AS), (c) SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015, (d) Secretarial Standards issued 
by the Institute of Company Secretaries of India.
The sustainability KPIs are disclosed in detail on our website 
through ESG Report and the GRI index.
Assurance and accountability approach

S.R. Batliboi & Associates LLP , our Statutory Auditor. BSI Group 
India Private Limited has issued a report on limited assurance 
for Sustainability disclosures and reasonable assurance for the 
Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report. The Board 
of Directors and Management have reviewed and affirmed the 
accuracy, completeness and integrity of the material information 
contained in this Report.Our Integrated Annual Report, aligned with the International 
Integrated Reporting Council ('IIRC'), sums up our financial as 
well as non-financial performance during the year, and informs 
all our stakeholders about our governance practices, material 
issues, risks, opportunities, strategy and prospects. 
Through this Report we are sharing Tata Communications’ vision 
for digital transformation, aligning with our overarching purpose, 
strategy and business model. We are providing here a transparent 
overview of how we create value for our stakeholders across the 
short, medium and long-term through the Company’s financial, 
environmental and societal activities.

Powering the Digital Future
Tata Communications is a leading global communications technology player 
powering today’s fast-growing digital economy. We simplify complexity, enhance 
security and elevate digital experiences, empowering businesses to thrive in the 
digital-first era.
We lead with trust, enabling digital transformation for 
enterprises worldwide through core and next-generation 
connectivity, cloud hosting and cybersecurity solutions, 
collaboration and connected solutions, and media services. 
Our digital fabric of solutions brings advanced platforms, tools 
and technologies to simplify complexity and enable enterprises 
to unlock new possibilities in a fast-evolving digital landscape.
We combine global network strength, innovation-led 
capabilities and a customer-centric approach to enable 
enterprises to operate securely, seamlessly and at scale in a 
hyperconnected world. Aligned with our focus on innovation 
and sustainability, our efforts are directed towards to reducing 
environmental impact, promoting inclusive growth and 
creating long-term value for all stakeholders.
Our strategy is guided by a clear sense of direction and shared values that shape how we operate, innovate and create value.

Because the Next Phase is Integrated
Businesses today do not just need connectivity. They need a simple way to bring 
together their people, applications, data and customers across many systems. This is 
where the shift from fiber to fabric becomes important. Fiber built the foundation. 
Fabric brings everything together into a single, integrated layer, where network, 
cloud, interaction and intelligence capabilities work together, enabling enterprises to 
operate seamlessly, respond faster to change and scale with greater efficiency.
Built on  
Reach
Tata Communications is built on a strong connectivity 
heritage that has enabled us to reach and connect enterprises 
across geographies. For years, this infrastructure helped our 
customers move data, run operations and stay connected in 
an increasingly borderless world. But as enterprises became 
more digital, their needs changed. Enterprises no longer 
wanted just connectivity; they demanded intelligent, agile, 
secure digital infrastructure.
Reimagined for  
Relevance
We sharpened our operating model, improved 
financial discipline and simplified how we 
worked. We moved away from a product-led 
approach and began solving larger enterprise 
problems. The focus shifted from selling separate 
services to creating integrated solutions that 
could support how modern enterprises operate, 
scale and compete. The launch of the Re-
imagine strategy marked a clear shift towards 
platforms and solutions. We transitioned from a 
connectivity-led network provider to a platform-
led communications technology company. Strength to Scale.  
Scale to Grow
As customer needs became more complex, we expanded 
our role. We were no longer only carrying enterprise 
traffic. We were helping customers in navigating 
changes across cloud, cybersecurity, IoT , media, 
mobility, and customer-interaction platforms. Capability 
investments and acquisitions, such as The SwitchTM and 
KaleyraTM helped us deepen our digital portfolio and 
move closer to the business needs of global enterprises.
Our journey has moved through two clear phases. In the 
first phase, we became financially fit. We built a more 
disciplined balance sheet and strengthened the business 
from within. In the second phase, we used that strength 
to invest organically and inorganically in capabilities that 
could shape our digital fabric. We are now entering the 
next phase, where the priority is profitable growth built on 
relevance, scale and deeper customer adoption.2016

Letter from 
the Chairman
Balancing Resilience 
with Ambitiondecisively from data and insights to real-time, intelligent 
action, while reinforcing trust and scalability in increasingly  
AI-driven ecosystems.
Trust as a Guiding Principle
As digital systems become more deeply embedded within 
enterprise, the role of trust becomes paramount.
For Tata Communications, trust of our customers and other 
stakeholders has always been foundational. Today, this extends 
across areas such as governance, cybersecurity, data protection 
and responsible technology deployment.
In a world where expectations continue to evolve, our 
commitment to integrity and transparency remains a defining 
strength. It is through such consistency that enduring 
stakeholder confidence is built and sustained.
This trust is reflected in an industry-leading Net Promoter Score 
of 83 (and 95 in the India market) a golden benchmark among 
our global peer group. These are not metrics to be reported 
and moved past. They represent the voice of our customers, 
and they affirm that your Company's growth strategy of 
migrating customers to higher value bands while maintaining 
uncompromising execution is working precisely as intended.
Sustainability: A Responsibility We Embrace
Your Company continues to advance its commitment to 
sustainable and inclusive growth. In alignment with Project 
Aalingana, the Tata Group’s unified commitment towards Driving 
Net Zero, Pioneering Circular Economy and Preserving Nature & 
Biodiversity, your Company continues to make steady progress 
across climate action, resource stewardship and community 
resilience initiatives.
Internally, your Company is taking decisive steps to reduce its 
environmental footprint. Our pledge to achieve Net Zero across 
global operations by 2035 is not an aspiration, it is an anchor 
for every decision we make. During the year, we continued to 
expand renewable energy adoption, improve energy efficiency 
and advance low-carbon transition initiatives, driving reductions 
in operational emissions intensity. We also strengthened our 
circularity and biodiversity efforts through achievement of Zero 
Waste to Landfill and biodiversity baseline assessment initiatives 
at our Pune campus for habitat improvement.
Your Company also continued to deepen its commitment towards 
preserving nature and strengthening ecological resilience 
through water stewardship, biodiversity and community-led 
conservation initiatives. Programmes such as Vitalize Rural, 
Nanneer and Project Sahjeevan contributed towards water 
replenishment, habitat restoration and renewable energy 
access in vulnerable communities. These efforts were further 
strengthened through disaster risk reduction frameworks and 
targeted mental and social well-being interventions, reinforcing 
community resilience for the long term.Leade rship Transition
The year marks an important change in leadership.
On behalf of the Board, I would like to express our 
sincere appreciation and heartfelt gratitude to Mr. A.S. 
Lakshminarayanan who retired this year after over 7 years of 
extraordinary leadership as Managing Director and CEO. Under 
his stewardship, your Company achieved remarkable milestones, 
and his strategic clarity, personal integrity and deep dedication 
have left a lasting and positive impact on our organisation. 
It is with equal warmth that I welcome Mr. Ganesh 
Lakshminarayanan as Managing Director and Chief Executive 
Officer. He assumes leadership at a time of significant 
opportunity, supported by a strong foundation built 
over the years. 
I would also like to recognise the contributions of Mr. Kabir 
Ahmed Shakir, whose leadership as Chief Financial Officer 
has helped strengthen your Company’s financial discipline 
and resilience during a period of significant transformation. 
I am equally pleased to welcome Mr. Siddhartha Mundra as 
Chief Financial Officer. He brings strong experience and a 
clear perspective, as we continue to build on your Company’s 
financial and strategic priorities.
The Board looks forward to the fresh energy that will be infused 
by Ganesh and Siddhartha’s leadership as we write the next 
chapter together.
Looking Ahead
The path ahead presents both opportunities and challenges.
The opportunity has never been greater. Demand for secure, 
scalable and intelligent digital capabilities is expected to 
continue growing, even as global uncertainties persist. 
Our path forward is guided by the same principles that have 
always defined us: relentless innovation, a genuine commitment 
to our customers, and the determination to build a sustainable 
future, for our business, our communities, and our planet. I 
remain deeply confident in our ability to create meaningful and 
lasting value for every stakeholder who places their trust in 
Tata Communications.
Finally, I am deeply grateful to our shareholders, customers, 
partners and employees. Your continued support and belief in 
Tata Communications are what make all of this possible. The 
best, I am certain, is yet to come.
The journey ahead will require both resolve and foresight—
and I am certain that your Company will continue to rise 
to the occasion.
In doing so, we remain guided by the enduring principle that 
business must create value not only for itself, but for the 
communities and stakeholders it serves—reinforcing trust, 
responsibility and purpose at every step.
Warm regards,
N. Ganapathy Subramaniam
ChairmanI am pleased to share with you the Integrated Annual Report for 
financial year 25–26.
This has been a year of purposeful progress: A year in which 
your Company not only delivered strong results but also 
deepened its strategic foundations, sharpened its focus on 
innovation, and demonstrated, once again, that resilience and 
ambition can thrive together.
As the world around us grows more complex, shaped by rapid 
technological change, shifting geopolitical currents, and 
evolving enterprise needs, I am proud to report that your 
Company has remained firmly on course: clear in its direction, 
confident in its capabilities, and committed to creating enduring 
value for every one of its stakeholders.
Performance: Resilience in a Testing Environment
Operating in an increasingly dynamic global environment, your 
Company delivered a consolidated revenue from operations of  
H24,803 crore for FY 25–26. The performance was strengthened 
by the continued momentum of our data and digital portfolio.
The Board has accordingly proposed a dividend of H17.50 per 
share for FY 25–26, subject to shareholder approval. This 
reflects your Company's financial discipline and its commitment 
to rewarding the trust you place in us.
Macroeconomic headwinds and geopolitical disruptions, 
including the continued uncertainty arising from the conflict 
in West Asia, have introduced caution into global IT spending. 
Yet, your Company has navigated these conditions with 
characteristic resilience, drawing on the depth of its capabilities 
and the enduring trust of its customers across all segments of 
its digital fabric. We remain confident in our ability to continue 
converting challenge into opportunity by demonstrating value 
to our customers.A Company Built for What's Next
We are focused on making businesses stronger by enabling 
seamless connectivity, securing critical operations, and 
advancing the technologies shaping the future. This remains the 
standard we bring to every client, across every market.
At the core of this is the Company’s digital fabric – an 
integrated architecture spanning network, cloud, security, 
and collaboration. It brings these capabilities together into a 
unified ecosystem that reduces complexity, optimises costs, 
and enables scalable growth. Built for current demands and 
designed to evolve, it is becoming a preferred platform for 
enterprises. With a clear focus on emerging technologies, 
intelligent systems, operational efficiency and responsible 
growth, your Company is well positioned to support enterprises 
in their digital evolution, both in India and globally.
We are seeing a fundamental shift in how enterprises operate. 
Hybrid cloud, AI, IoT , edge computing and security are no longer 
emerging trends but core to business strategy. Among these, AI 
will be a defining force in the years ahead.
Your Company is approaching this shift with discipline, focusing 
not just on capability expansion, but on ensuring innovation is 
underpinned by governance, security, and accountability.
During the year, your Company advanced its AI-ready portfolio 
with a clear strategic focus on helping enterprises adopt AI with 
confidence and clarity. Our platforms, built on our digital fabric 
are designed to simplify complexity, integrate capabilities and 
enable more intelligent operations across environments.
We also strengthened our position through targeted innovations 
and partnerships, including enhanced network capabilities, 
AI-led orchestration and collaboration with global technology 
leaders. These efforts are enabling enterprises to move more Dear Shareholders,With a clear focus on emerging

Message from the  
Managing Director & CEO
Together, Enabling a  
Limitless TomorrowReimagining the AI Era
Our progress is best understood through the evolution of each 
layer of our digital fabric.
Network Fabric: Our Network Fabric remains the backbone of 
our portfolio, evolving beyond high-performance connectivity 
into an intelligent, programmable and self-healing network. 
During FY 25-26, we expanded AI-enabled automation to 
enable real-time optimisation, faster fault resolution and 
improved service resilience for global enterprises. Network-
led data revenues continue to anchor our performance. 
Cloud Fabric: Our Cloud and Security Fabric continues 
to enable enterprises to securely connect and manage 
increasingly distributed workloads across hybrid and multi 
cloud environments. Growth in our Digital Portfolio was 
driven by rising adoption of secure cloud networking, Secure 
Access Service Edge ('SASE')-aligned architectures and 
sovereign infrastructure. 
Interaction Fabric: Our Interaction Fabric has emerged as 
a key growth engine, strengthened by KaleyraTM and further 
accelerated by the acquisition of Commotion. This has 
significantly enhanced our capabilities in AI-led customer 
engagement, spanning voice AI, automation, personalisation 
and real-time orchestration across channels. While still 
at an early stage, Commotion strengthens our ability to 
deliver outcome-led, AI-powered solutions and deepens our 
participation in the evolving enterprise AI ecosystem.
What is changing, however, is not just the strength of 
each fabric, but how they are converging into a single, AI 
embedded platform - the digital fabric operating as one.
ThreadSpan™: We launched ThreadSpan™ as a key pillar 
of our AI-ready portfolio, designed to simplify the growing 
complexity of hybrid and multi cloud environments. By 
continuously discovering and correlating data across systems, 
it enables real-time decision-making, reduces operational 
complexity and strengthens resilience, providing enterprises 
with a single, integrated control plane to securely scale AI-
driven and data-intensive workloads.It is both a privilege and a moment of great responsibility for 
me to address you for the first time as Managing Director and 
Chief Executive Officer of Tata Communications as I present

Building on a Strong Foundation
FY 25–26 has been a year of steady progress and disciplined 
execution. We continued to invest in strengthening our digital 
platforms, enhancing capabilities and building long-term 
growth engines.
Tata Communications has delivered a resilient financial 
performance, with revenue of H24,803 crore from consolidated 
operations, reflecting a steady growth of 7.3% year-on-year. 
Revenue from our data business grew 9.4% to H21,352 crore. 
Our digital portfolio continues to be a key driver of this progress, contributing nearly 50% of our revenue with an 
expansion of 16.7% during the year, supported by increasing 
enterprise adoption, deeper customer engagement and 
strong deal momentum across geographies. Importantly, 
we saw a sharp improvement in free cash flow to H1,474 
crore and continued strengthening of our balance sheet, 
with net debt-to-EBITDA falling below 2x. These outcomes 
reflect a consistent approach to balancing growth with 
financial discipline.
Evolving with Our Customers

central to enabling customers in the AI era. A defining theme 
emerging from my interactions has been the changing nature 
of enterprise transformation. Organisations are not just 
digitising, they are rethinking their operating models.
Two powerful forces are shaping this transition:
	yIn emerging markets, the consumer front end is digitised 
but the real opportunities lies in digitisation of the supply 
chain – factories, warehouses and logistics.
	yIn developed markets, the focus is shifting towards AI-led 
transformation. The most compelling AI ROI will come 
from enterprise intelligence-AI applied to proprietary 
enterprise data.
This is where Tata Communications is uniquely positioned. 
Our network backbone along with our cloud and security

balance global scale with local sovereignty.

A Five-Year Financial Journey: From Stability to Scalable Growth
Over the last five years, Tata Communications has 
progressively reshaped its financial profile to support a 
changing business mix. During this period, the focus was 
on strengthening cash flows, managing leverage prudently 
and maintaining resilience amid external disruptions such 
as cable outages, geopolitical uncertainties and fluctuating 
enterprise demand.
As the digital portfolio expanded, spanning cloud, 
cybersecurity, customer interaction, IoT , mobility and media, 
the Company entered a focused investment phase. Guided 
by ‘Fit to Grow’ and ‘Fit to Compete’, the two pillars of our financial fitness model, capital was allocated towards building 
product capability, launching new platforms and acquiring 
strategic assets. While some of these investments impacted 
near term margins, they were undertaken with defined paths 
to profitability and clear return thresholds.
This transition has resulted in a more balanced revenue mix 
today, with digital portfolio now contributing meaningfully 
alongside core connectivity. Importantly, the quality and 
visibility of revenues have improved through greater 
platform based, enterprise led engagements and a growing 
international order book.

Financial Performance in FY 25-26
In FY 25-26, Data Revenue increased to H 21,352 crore from H 19,513 crore in FY 24-25, reflecting sustained growth in the Company’s 
digital portfolio and continued adoption of its digital fabric solutions. Profit After Tax ('PAT') declined to H 1,044 crore compared to  
H1,625 crore in FY 25, with PAT margin moderating from 7.0% to 4.2%, primarily due to the impact of a non-recurring income from land 
monetisation recorded in the previous year.
The underlying operating performance remained stable, with EBITDA margins largely sustained. Net debt to EBITDA improved further, 
closing below 2.0x in FY 25-26, supported by prudent capital allocation, strong operating cash flows and disciplined balance sheet 
management.Strengthening Revenue Visibility and Quality
Over recent years, the enterprise order book has grown at 
a healthy pace, with the digital portfolio accounting for an 
increasing share. Digital platforms allow us to deepen our 
relationships with customers, increasing our relevance to them. 
This improves structured financial planning and visibility.
International operations continue to play a critical role in 
strengthening scale, diversification and visibility. Investment 
decisions have been guided with a clear focus on profitability 
thresholds, operating leverage and working capital 
discipline, ensuring growth does not come at the expense of 
financial stability.

Planning
Financial planning at Tata Communications incorporates 
structured scenario analysis and both long-range and short-
range planning cycles. In a year characterised by evolving 
macroeconomic conditions and heightened market volatility, 
maintaining financial resilience required planned strategic 
interventions. Through structured planning frameworks and 
robust cost governance, we continued to safeguard margins, 
preserve cash flows and sustain operating stability, while 
supporting ongoing investments in our digital capabilities.
We have a comprehensive and disciplined approach to 
financial management by evaluating multiple operating 
scenarios and evolving market conditions to proactively 
anticipate change and enable timely strategic responses. 
This is supported by continuous performance monitoring that 
allows us to assess outcomes against market dynamics and 
recalibrate plans as needed.

Enhancing the shareholder experience
Enhancing the experience of our shareholders in interactions with 
the Company remains an important focus area for us. Technology 
enabled platforms and responsive service models such as Investor 
Relations Contact Centres and a 24/7 AI-enabled Chatbot 
maintained by our Registrar and Transfer Agent are used to make 
interactions simpler, faster and more accessible. These efforts are 
aimed at improving ease of engagement, strengthening service 
delivery and ensuring timely resolution of shareholder queries.
During the year, our efforts were aligned with regulatory 
initiatives led by SEBI and the Investor Education and Protection 
Fund Authority, including the Saksham Niveshak campaign. This 
nationwide initiative focused on investor awareness, KYC and 
nomination updates, and facilitating the claim of unclaimed 
dividends. The initiative received encouraging participation 
and positive feedback from shareholders, reflecting improved 
awareness, timely compliance and stronger engagement.

Strengthening Cybersecurity 
Resilience for Kotak Mahindra Asset 
Management Company ('KMAMC')
Part of the Kotak Mahindra Group, KMAMC offers mutual 
fund and investment solutions across equity, debt, hybrid 
and alternative asset classes, serving individual and 
institutional investors.
Business Challenge
KMAMC’s cybersecurity approach was largely reactive, 
with manual monitoring, limited real-time threat visibility 
and delayed incident response. In a highly regulated BFSI 
environment, the organisation needed a more proactive, 
intelligence-led security model to strengthen resilience, 
accountability and business continuity.
Key OutcomesOur Solution
We implemented a Managed Security Information and Event 
Management ('SIEM') solution, later expanded with Security 
Orchestration, Automation and Response ('SOAR'), and User 
and Entity Behaviour Analytics ('UEBA') capabilities. Through 
a phased rollout, we helped KMAMC move from reactive 
monitoring to a proactive, intelligence-led security model.
Key capabilities delivered included:

messagingCustomer Interaction Suite ('CIS'): From 
Conversations to Autonomous Journeys
Our Customer Interaction Suite sits at the core of the 
Interaction Fabric and represents Tata Communications’ key 
priorities in experience led growth.
Built on the foundation of Kaleyra and strengthened by 
the acquisition of Commotion Inc., CIS has evolved from a 
multichannel engagement platform into a unified, AI-powered 
platform for customer experience and journey orchestration.
At its core, CIS integrates communication channels, customer 
data, analytics and agentic AI to enable enterprises to design, 
manage and continuously optimise end-to-end customer 
journeys. The addition of Commotion brings an orchestration 
and automation layer that enables AI not only to respond 
but also to interpret intent, understand context and execute 
across workflows with governance and human oversight.
This evolution enables a step change for enterprises:AI-led Experience and Operations
AI is deeply embedded across CIS to drive measurable 
improvements in experience and efficiency. Conversational 
AI, analytics and orchestration operate as a continuous 
loop, interpreting intent, determining next best actions and 
executing workflows in real time.

Beyond customer engagement, agentic AI has also transformed

observability and enabling predictive, self optimising 
support models.
Unified Communications as a Service ('UCaaS'): 
Enabling Consistent Collaboration at a  
Global Scale
While customer engagement and connected ecosystems 
build enterprise interaction, internal collaboration remains 
a critical enabler of productivity, resilience and experience 
delivery. Our Interaction Fabric supports large scale, global 
workforce collaboration through a managed, platform 
agnostic UCaaS model.
Tata Communications' UCaaS enables enterprises to standardise 
voice and collaboration services across regions while navigating 
the complexity of multi platform adoption, regulatory diversity 
and rapid workforce scaling. Anchored in robust global voice 
infrastructure and end to end lifecycle management, these 
offerings support the full journey, from assessment and 
migration to provisioning, monitoring and ongoing optimisation.
Simplifying Collaboration Across Platforms and 
Geographies
We operate in increasingly multi-vendor collaboration 
environments, with enterprises adopting platforms such as 
Microsoft Teams, Webex Calling, Zoom Phone and Google 
Workspace. Through our UCaaS offerings, we bring these 
disparate ecosystems together under a single, managed 
framework, integrating cloud, voice, Public Switched 
Telephone Network (PSTN) services, numbering, devices and 
meeting room infrastructure.
This vendor agnostic approach provides flexibility to evolve 
collaboration strategies without operational disruption. 
By combining global PSTN coverage with platform native 
models such as Operator Connect and Direct Routing, we 
significantly accelerate deployment timelines. Apart from 
reducing rollouts from months to weeks, it also ensures 
consistent performance and policy control across locations.
Resilient, Secure and Compliant by Design
We have built our UCaaS offerings on Tata Communications’ 
carrier grade global network, enabling high availability 
voice services at scale. Through centralised monitoring, 
proactive analytics and automated workflows, we strengthen 
reliability, improve visibility and accelerate issue resolution, 
particularly in high volume enterprise environments.
In addition, security and compliance are embedded across 
the solution. Capabilities such as Fraud Protection as a 
Service ('FPaaS') provide real time anomaly detection and 
automated mitigation, while unified numbering governance 
ensures compliance with country specific regulations across 
markets. As a single global voice provider, we simplify 
operations by removing the complexity of managing multiple 
local carriers and regulatory frameworks.
Retail Banking Contact Centre 
Transformation
Business Challenge
A major retail banking organisation serving over 21 
million customers was supported by an extensive 
agent network operating through fragmented legacy 
processes. This resulted in slow service cycles, high 
manual dependency, limited scalability and challenges 
in meeting evolving customer experience expectations 
while ensuring GDPR compliance.
Our Solution
We delivered a cloud-native Contact Centre as a 
Service (CCaaS) transformation, consolidating legacy 
processes into a unified omnichannel platform. The 
solution integrated AI capabilities such as Voice Bots, 
Agent Copilot, predictive analytics and automated 
workflows, along with a unified agent desktop to 
streamline operations.
Key Outcomes
The transformation improved operational efficiency and 
customer experience while reducing manual workload. 
It enabled faster response times, improved agent 
productivity and ensured secure, compliant operations.

Our CSR Strategy: Kairos in Action 
Our community initiatives are guided by Kairos, our 
integrated CSR strategy inspired by the Greek concept of 
καιρός—the right, opportune moment—focused on delivering 
meaningful, scalable and long-term impact.
Kairos is anchored in two core pillars—sustainable 
livelihoods and environmental stewardship—supported 
by education, technology and well-being as key enablers 
and Affirmative Action communities as priority. Employee 
volunteering, innovation and climate action cut across all 
initiatives, ensuring that our programmes remain inclusive, 
scalable and aligned to broader business priorities. As an  
extension to our strategy, this year, we launched an  
intervention Zehn Ki Lehar, which focuses on the mental  
and social well-being of our existing project participants.During the year, our community initiatives focused on addressing ecological degradation, economic exclusion, environmental 
vulnerability and unequal access to opportunity, through programmes that are scalable, inclusive and measurable in impact. In 
addition, we supported initiatives that enable safer, more resilient co-existence between communities and the natural ecosystems 
they inhabit. These interventions were further strengthened through the integration of disaster risk reduction (DRR) frameworks 
and targeted actions to support mental and social well-being, reinforcing community resilience and long-term sustainability.

Rejuvenating Lives 
Launched in 2022, Project Nanneer by Tata Communications 
revitalised the Nagan Thangal Lake, transforming a degraded 
waterbody into a thriving ecological and community asset. 
The intervention tripled lake storage capacity, improved 
groundwater recharge and reduced surrounding barren 
land, while restoring local biodiversity. Today, the lake 
supports the revival of 14 Fish species, 56 Bird species 
and 33 Butterfly species , strengthening water security, 
ecosystem health and community engagement. Nagan 
Thangal Lake, at full capacity, preserves 1,078 tCO2e

Health, Safety and Well-being
At Tata Communications, the health, safety and well 
being of every employee is non negotiable. We adopt a 
zero tolerance approach to unsafe practices supported 
by structured governance, proactive interventions and 
increasing use of digital tools.
Beyond physical safety, employee well being is supported 
through initiatives addressing mental, emotional and social 
health. The Recharge Squad, an employee led volunteer 
network, drives community building and well-being 
initiatives across global locations, reinforcing a supportive 
and connected workplace.Safety in Every Setting
Health and safety at Tata Communications is guided by 
three core pillars: risk mitigation, employee well-being 
and technology-enabled governance.  Together, they ensure 
consistent standards across offices, field operations and 
remote work environments. 
Risk Mitigation and Hazard Control
Structured Hazard Identification and Risk Assessments help 
identify risks early and embed controls into daily operations. 
High-risk activities are managed through Mandatory 
Safety Standards, a digital Permit-to-Work system and the 
e-Safety Passport, which validates training before critical 
tasks are assigned.
Employee Health and Well-being
Safe and healthy workplaces are enabled through ergonomic 
assessments, indoor air quality checks, fire readiness and safety 
inductions. Mental health programmes, wellness initiatives and 
awareness sessions further support employee well-being.
Technology-enabled Governance
Digital tools strengthen transparency and accountability across 
the safety ecosystem. Online permit to work, mobile hazard 
reporting, digital audits and competency tracking help improve 
traceability, response and governance across work environments.

Advancing Climate Action and Decarbonisation
Addressing climate change remains a key priority for Tata 
Communications. Our climate strategy is anchored in a clear 
decarbonisation pathway, with an aim to achieve Carbon 
neutrality by 2030 and Net-Zero emissions (Scope 1, 2 
and 3) by 2035. 
Progress is guided by global frameworks, including the 
GHG Protocol and Science Based Targets initiative, 
and strengthened through scenario-based climate 
risk assessments.Integrating our Sustainability Strategy into 
decision-making
Sustainability at Tata Communications is not treated as a 
parallel initiative but is embedded into our core business 
and financial frameworks. This integration ensures that 
environmental performance directly influences operational 
decisions, capital deployment and risk management. This 
has sharpened internal focus on measurable reductions and 
strengthened cross-functional accountability.

Community-based Offsets and Local Impact
Our community-based carbon offset programmes support 
our carbon neutrality goals while also creating meaningful 
benefits for local communities.
Agroforestry initiatives help generate livelihoods, while 
improved cookstove projects reduce indoor air pollution 
and improve household health. These initiatives have been 
registered under Verra’s Verified Carbon Standard and 
also generate verified carbon credits, which help offset 
greenhouse gas emissions.
By reducing dependence on traditional biomass, these 
programmes contribute to cleaner air and healthier living 
conditions. The carbon credits generated are fully traceable 
and aligned with recognised global standards.
We select and scale these nature-based, community-led 
initiatives based on local needs, with ongoing monitoring to 
ensure they deliver both environmental and social impact.Community Water Replenishment Initiatives
Chennai, Tamil Nadu
Since 2022, lake rejuvenation 
efforts at Nagan Thangal lake 
have enhanced water holding 
capacity and supported 
groundwater recharge. 
The initiative has also 
contributed to biodiversity 
revival and created a shared 
community space centred on 
water conservation.
Water Stewardship and Resource Conservation
Responsible water management remains a priority, 
particularly in water stressed locations. Site level monitoring, 
IoT enabled tracking and preventive maintenance help us 
improve visibility and reduce consumption. Increased use 
of recycled water and rainwater harvesting contributes 
to improved water efficiency and reduced dependence on 
freshwater sources.
Investments in rainwater harvesting, recycling systems 
and watershed development enhance resource efficiency 
while contributing to long-term water security. Our push 
towards water neutrality combines operational efficiency 
with community based replenishment initiatives, supporting 
long term water security for both our operations and 
surrounding communities.Waste Management and Circular Economy
Waste management practices at our facilities continue to 
mature through improved segregation, centralised tracking 
and partnerships with authorised recyclers. A strong focus on 
reducing non biodegradable waste and improving recycling 
rates supports circular economy principles across offices and 
operational sites.
E-waste, battery waste and hazardous materials are 
managed through compliant, traceable processes aligned 
with Extended Producer Responsibility requirements. These 
measures ensure environmental protection while maintaining 
regulatory compliance across geographies.

Information Security and Data Privacy: Enabling  
Digital Trust
As a global digital infrastructure provider, trust is fundamental to 
our business. Information security and data privacy are therefore 
embedded as core pillars of our governance framework.
Privacy by Design
We have embedded privacy-by-design principles across 
our products, services, and processes. Each initiative 
undergoes structured privacy impact assessments to ensure 
alignment with regulatory requirements and the safeguarding 
of personal data.
Our key capabilities include:
Clearly defined processes for managing data subject rights, 
ensuring transparency and regulatory compliance
Comprehensive data lifecycle management, spanning data 
collection, storage, usage, and secure disposal
Deployment of privacy controls supported by periodic 
reporting to Management and the Board, enabling proactive 
oversight and accountability
Robust Cybersecurity Framework

priorities and built on the following principles:
Proactive identification and effective management of

Continuous innovation to address evolving business and 
threat landscapes

Navigating Risk with Confidence
At Tata Communications, our risk management approach is anchored in a 
structured, forward-looking framework that adapts to an increasingly dynamic 
environment. Operating across diverse geographies, we continuously track external 
developments to stay prepared for potential disruptions and ensure business 
continuity. This approach enables us to remain resilient and deliver consistently 
on our commitments. By embedding risk into strategic and operational decision-
making, supported by a strong governance framework, we reinforce agility and 
stability in executing our growth strategy.
Risk Integration and Monitoring
Risk insights are embedded into our strategic and operational 
decision-making, ensuring that business priorities are aligned 
with a clear understanding of exposures and mitigation 
actions. Continuous capability-building initiatives, including 
focused risk champion programmes, foster a strong risk-
aware culture and enhance responsiveness across functions. 
Structured surveillance mechanisms, through quarterly 
and event-driven reviews with business risk owners, 
provide ongoing visibility into risk exposure, severity and 
mitigation progress. 
In addition, continuous tracking of key geopolitical and 
macroeconomic developments enables early identification 
of potential disruptions and supports timely responses, 
strengthening organisational resilience and continuity.
During the year, early-warning indicators were also reviewed 
across key geopolitical and macroeconomic developments, 
including potential tariff changes in the United States 
and Mexico, Indo-Pak tensions, China’s rare earth export 
controls, instability in the Middle East and the Red Sea 
cable cut incident.Strategic Risk

uncertainties may affect our operations across multiple geographies.

17.  Dematerialisation of Shares
 As per R egulation 40 of the SEBI Listing Regulations, as 
amended, securities of listed companies can be transferred, 
transmitted and transposed only in dematerialised form. 
In view of this and to eliminate all risks associated with 
physical shares and for ease of portfolio management, 
Members holding shares in physical form are requested 
to consider converting their holdings to dematerialised 
form. Members can contact the RTA at investor.helpdesk@
in.mpms.mufg.com  for assistance in this regard.
 Attention 
of Members is also drawn to the SEBI circular 
dated January 25, 2022 mandating all listed entities 
to issue securities in dematerialised form only while processing service requests relating to issue of duplicate 
securities certificate, claim from unclaimed suspense 
account renewal / exchange of securities certificate, 
endorsement, sub-division / splitting of securities 
certificate, consolidation of securities certificates / folios, 
transposition and transmission. Accordingly, Members 
are requested to submit duly filled Form ISR-4 or Form 
ISR-5, as applicable, for the above-mentioned requests 
and surrender their original securities certificate(s) for 
processing of service requests to the RTA. 
 With effect from April 2, 2026, SEBI has dispensed with 
the requirement of issuance of a Letter of Confirmation   
by the Company / RTA while processing service requests. 
Accordingly, securities will be credited directly to the 
Member’s demat account upon submission of valid demat 
account details along with the latest Client Master List.

Explanatory Statement
Pursuant to Section 102(1) of the Companies Act, 2013 
(‘Act’) the following Explanatory Statement sets out material 
facts relating to business mentioned under Item Nos. 5 and 6 
of the accompanying Notice.
In respect of Item No. 5
Under the provisions of Section 148 of the Act read with the 
Companies (Cost Records and Audit) Rules, 2014, as amended, 
the Company is required to have its cost records audited by a 
Cost Accountant. In accordance with the provisions of Section 
148 of the Act read with the Companies (Audit and Auditors) 
Rules, 2014, the remuneration payable to the Cost Auditor is 
required to be ratified by the Members of the Company.
The Board, on the recommendation of the Audit Committee, 
has approved the appointment and remuneration of Ms. Ketki 
D. Visariya, Cost Accountant, as Cost Auditor to conduct the 
audit of the cost records of the Company for the financial year 
ending March 31, 2027 at a remuneration of H6.60 lakhs plus 
applicable taxes and out of pocket expenses on actual basis 
capped at 3% of the remuneration.
Accordingly, consent of the Members is sought by way of an 
Ordinary Resolution as set out at Item No. 5 of the accompanying 
Notice for ratification of the remuneration payable to the Cost 
Auditor for the financial year ending March 31, 2027.
The Board recommends the Ordinary Resolution set out at Item 
No. 5 of the Notice for approval by the Members.
None of the Directors and Key Managerial Personnel (‘KMP’) or 
their respective relatives are concerned or interested in the 
Resolution at Item No. 5 of the accompanying Notice.
In respect of Item No. 6
The Nomination and Remuneration Committee (‘NRC’), at 
its meeting held on January 21, 2026, recommended to the 
Board, the name of Mr. Ganapathi S. Lakshminarayanan (DIN: 
01828104) for appointment as Managing Director and Chief 
Executive Officer (‘MD & CEO’) of the Company. Based on the 
NRC’s recommendation, the Board of Directors, at its meeting 
held on January 21, 2026, had appointed Mr. Ganapathi S. 
Lakshminarayanan as the MD & CEO – Designate, subject to 
receipt of necessary regulatory approval. Thereafter, in 
accordance with the terms of its TV uplinking license, the 
Company had applied to the Ministry of Information and 
Broadcasting (‘MIB’) for obtaining its permission for the 
said appointment.Vide letter dated May 19, 2026, the Company received approval 
from MIB for appointment of Mr. Lakshminarayanan as MD & 
CEO. The Company has also received the necessary consent 
and declarations from Mr. Lakshminarayanan confirming his 
eligibility to be appointed as the MD & CEO.
The NRC, at its meeting held on May 20, 2026, in terms of 
Section 161 of the Act and applicable rules thereunder, 
recommended appointment of Mr. Lakshminarayanan as an 
Additional Director and as the MD & CEO of the Company.
Based on the aforementioned recommendation and 
approvals, the Board of Directors at its meeting held on 
May 20, 2026 approved the appointment of Mr. Ganapathi S. 
Lakshminarayanan (DIN: 01828104) as an Additional Director 
and as MD & CEO of the Company, to hold office for a term 
of five consecutive years with effect from May 20, 2026 up to 
May 19, 2031 (both days inclusive), subject to approval of the 
Members and other applicable regulatory approval from the 
Government of India and all other statutory authorities, if any.
The Company has received notice under section 160 of the 
Act proposing his candidature as Director of the Company. If 
appointed, Mr. Lakshminarayanan will act as MD & CEO, not 
liable to retire by rotation.

Company’s Performance
FY 2025–26 reflected sustained progress, driven by disciplined 
execution of the Company’s strategic priorities. The Company 
strengthened and invested in its digital platforms, enhancing 
capabilities in line with evolving digital and AI-led industry 
trends, while maintaining capital efficiency. Revenue from 
the data business increased by 9.4% to H21,352 crore. The 
digital portfolio remained a key contributor and grew by 16.7% 
during the year, driven by higher enterprise adoption, deeper 
customer engagement and strong deal wins across geographies.During the year under review, the Company undertook key 
strategic initiatives to further strengthen its digital fabric, 
including the acquisition of Commotion Inc., to enhance its 
Interaction Fabric. The Company also launched an AI-ready suite 
of platforms comprising Tata Communications IZO™+ Multi Cloud 
Network, Tata Communications Edge Distribution Platform and 
ThreadSpan™, built on its digital fabric of solutions. These 
offerings integrate network, cloud, cybersecurity and related 
capabilities, and are designed to support organisations in 
scaling the adoption of AI with confidence, control and clarity.

Internal Restructuring:
During FY 2025-26, your Company has undertaken various 
internal restructuring activities in the course of simplifying its 
existing layered group structure of subsidiaries, as follows:
1. Tata
 Communications SVCS Pte. Ltd., a step-down 
subsidiary of the Company, through an Intra-Group 
Business Transfer Agreement dated March 31, 2025, 
transferred its entire business to TC Networks Switzerland 
SA, another step-down subsidiary of the Company, 
effective April 1, 2025.
2. Pursuant to the 
investment made by the Company in Tata 
Communications (Netherlands) B.V. (‘TC Netherlands’) 
and subsequent buy back of its existing share capital, TC 
Netherlands became a direct wholly-owned subsidiary of 
the Company effective April 4, 2025.
3. In line 
with continued focus on portfolio optimisation and 
prioritising Digital Portfolio, Tata Communications divested 
its entire stake in NetFoundry Inc., during the year.
4. Tata
 Communications (Hong Kong) Limited, a step-down 
wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company, incorporated TC 
(Shanghai) Network Services Company Limited in People’s 
Republic of China as its wholly-owned subsidiary with 
effect from April 18, 2025.
5. Through an Intra-Group 
Share Purchase Agreement dated 
July 31, 2025, the Company acquired the entire equity 
share capital of its step-down wholly-owned subsidiary - 
Solutions Infini Technologies (India) Private Limited (‘SI 
India’) from Kaleyra S.p.A., thereby making it a direct 
wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company.
6. On January 22, 
2026, a composite scheme of arrangement 
for the demerger of SI India’s (‘Transferor Company’) 
non-licensed business undertaking into Novamesh Limited 
(‘Transferee Company’) and the subsequent amalgamation 
of SI India into Tata Communications Collaboration Services 
Private Limited (‘Surviving Company’) (‘Scheme’) was 
approved by the respective boards of directors of all the 
entities involved in the Scheme. The Transferor Company, 
Transferee Company and Surviving Company are wholly-
owned subsidiaries of the Company. The Scheme has been 
filed before the Mumbai Bench of the Hon’ble National Company Law Tribunal pursuant to Sections 230 to 232 
and all other applicable provisions of the Act.

Directors’ Responsibility Statement
Based on the framework of internal financial controls and 
compliance systems established and maintained by the 
Company, the work performed by the internal, statutory, cost 
and secretarial auditors and external consultants, including 
the audit of internal financial controls over financial reporting 
by the statutory auditor and the reviews performed by 
Management and the relevant Board committees, including 
the Audit Committee, the Board is of the opinion that the 
Company’s internal financial controls were adequate and 
effective during financial year 2025-26.
Pursuant to Section 134(5) of the Act, the Board of Directors, 
to the best of its knowledge and ability, confirm that for the 
year ended March 31, 2026:
i. In the 
preparation of the annual accounts, the applicable 
accounting standards have been followed and there are 
no material departures;
ii. They have 
selected such accounting policies and applied 
them consistently and made judgments and estimates 
that are reasonable and prudent so as to give a true and 
fair view of the state of affairs of the Company at the end 
of the financial year and of the profit of the Company 
for that period;
iii. They have taken 
proper and sufficient care for the 
maintenance of adequate accounting records in 
accordance with the provisions of the Act for safeguarding 
assets of the Company and for preventing and detecting 
fraud and other irregularities;As the Company enters FY 2026–27, it remains well positioned 
to participate in the next phase of growth, supported by 
expanding opportunities. The Company’s integrated digital 
offerings, growing AI-led capabilities and strong customer 
relationships provide a strong foundation for sustained growth 
and value creation. 
On a standalone basis, the revenue from operations for FY 2025-26  
was H7,375.71 crore, higher by 1.34% over the previous year’s 
revenue of H7,277.86 crore. Profit after tax (‘PAT’) attributable 
to shareholders for FY 2025-26 was H793.87 crore as compared 
to PAT of H1,050.87 crore for the previous year. The decline in 
standalone PAT is primarily due to strategic business divestments 
and real estate monetisation benefits in the previous year.
On a consolidated basis, the revenue from operations for 
FY 2025-26 was H24,802.72 crore, higher by 7.33% over the 
previous year’s revenue of H23,108.59 crore. PAT attributable to 
shareholders and non-controlling interests for FY 2025-26 was  
H996.85 crore as compared to H1,836.78 crore for the previous 
year. The decline in the consolidated PAT is majorly driven by 
certain real estate monetisation benefits in the previous year.
Dividend
The Board recommends a dividend of H17.50/- per fully paid 
equity share on 285,000,000 equity shares of face value H10/- 
each, for the financial year ended March 31, 2026. The Board 
has recommended dividend based on the parameters laid down 
in the Dividend Distribution Policy, which can be accessed at 
www.tatacommunications.com/resource/corporateresources/
policies/tcl-dividend-distribution-policy/ . 
The dividend on equity shares is subject to approval of the 
Members at the Annual General Meeting (‘AGM’) scheduled to 
be held on Thursday, July 9, 2026.
The dividend, once approved by the Members, will be paid, 
subject to deduction of tax at source, on or after Friday, July 
10, 2026. If approved, the dividend will result in a cash outflow 
of ~H499 crore. The dividend on equity shares is 175% of the 
paid-up value of each share. 
The Company has fixed Friday, June 19, 2026 as the ‘Record 
Date’ and will close the Register of Members from Saturday, 
June 20, 2026 till Tuesday, June 23, 2026 (both days inclusive) 
for determining entitlement of Members to final dividend for the 
financial year ended March 31, 2026, if approved at the AGM.

(Share Based Employee Benefits and Sweat Equity) Regulations, 
2021 (‘SBEB Regulations’). The Nomination and Remuneration 
Committee (‘NRC’) administers the Plan and functions as the

Eligible employees shall be granted RSUs, as determined by the 
NRC, which will vest as per the approved vesting schedule and 
are exercisable into fully paid-up equity shares of H10/- each 
of the Company, on the terms and conditions as provided under 
the Plan, in accordance with the provisions of applicable laws 
and regulations for the time being in force. During the year 
under review, 8,01,558 (Eight Lakh One Thousand Five Hundred 
and Fifty-Eight) RSUs were granted to eligible employees of the 
Company and its subsidiaries. These RSUs shall vest at the end 
of the Plan Period i.e., April 30, 2028, subject to fulfillment of 
defined conditions.

Environmental, Social and Governance (‘ESG’)
Sustainability at Tata Communications is driven by a well-
defined strategy that integrates environmental, social, 
and governance considerations into its core business model 
and long-term value creation approach. Our sustainability 
framework is anchored in a multi-pillar structure, typically 
encompassing environmental stewardship, trusted digital 
infrastructure, people and culture, and responsible business 
practices through People, Planet, Community and Governance.
Under the Planet pillar and environmental stewardship, Tata 
Communications focuses on reducing its carbon footprint 
through energy efficiency, increased adoption of renewable 
energy, and responsible resource management, aligning its 
actions with global frameworks such as the Global Reporting 
Initiative and the United Nations Sustainable Development 
Goals. Embedding circularity in our operations and optimisation 
of natural resource management is one of the key aspects of 
our commitment to sustainability.
On the social front, under the People and Community pillars, 
Tata Communications prioritises human capital development, 
diversity and inclusion, and employee well-being, business 
and human rights, while also advancing initiatives to address 
pressing issues such as education, sustainable livelihoods and 
positive environmental impact across communities. Responsible 
business practices form another key aspect covering value 
chain and sustainable supply chain management embedded 
across operations.
The Governance pillar reinforces trusted digital infrastructure 
emphasises robust cybersecurity, data privacy, and resilient 
network services, which are critical for maintaining customer 
trust in an increasingly digital world along with strong 
governance systems, ethical conduct, and adherence to 
regulatory compliance.
These pillars are supported by measurable targets, risk 
management processes, and continuous stakeholder 
engagement, ensuring that sustainability considerations are 
integrated into decision-making at all levels.
Looking ahead, Tata Communications is strengthening its 
sustainability strategy by setting more ambitious, science-
aligned targets and embedding ESG metrics deeper into 
business performance frameworks. The Company is working 
towards building a futuristic goal which includes accelerating 
decarbonisation pathways, expanding circular economy 
initiatives, implementing people centric initiatives that 
improve wellbeing, integrate innovative solutions to integrate 
sustainability into value chain operations, deepening its focus 
on human rights across the value chain, leverage future-
ready skills and enhancing community engagement through 
impactful projects. By advancing these strategic pillars, Tata Communications is 
positioning itself to not only mitigate risks but also unlock new 
opportunities, reinforcing its role as a responsible and future-
ready commtech player.
Our sustainability performance can be viewed on our website 
and in the BRSR and the Natural Capital section of this 
Integrated Annual Report.
Human Resources
At Tata Communications, our people remain central to our 
growth and transformation, and we are committed to creating 
a workplace where every employee feels valued, empowered, 
and inspired to perform at their best. We are focused on 
building a future-ready workforce that is technologically 
skilled, adaptable, and aligned with our purpose. Our human 
resource strategy emphasises strengthening digital and domain 
capabilities, fostering leadership, and enabling a collaborative 
and inclusive work environment. Through continued 
investments in skills, wellbeing, and professional growth, 
we aim to create a high-performance culture that supports 
innovation and delivers sustainable long-term value.
Our approach is anchored in three strategic pillars: compelling 
employees value proposition, smarter workforce planning and 
culture and social fabric. These are further strengthened by our 
global talent strategy that enables access to specialised skills 
across geographies through talent hubs in key global locations, 
digital sourcing and AI-enabled hiring, industry partnerships, 
flexible and hybrid work models.
To learn more about our employee engagement and 
development initiatives, please refer to ‘Our People’ section 
of this Integrated Annual Report.
Disclosures pertaining to the Sexual Harassment of 
Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and 
Redressal) Act, 2013
Tata Communications has zero tolerance for sexual harassment 
and has adopted a charter on prevention, prohibition and 
redressal of sexual harassment in line with the provisions of 
the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, 
Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 and complied with all 
provisions of the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace 
(Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013, including 
constitution of Internal Complaints Committee (‘ICC’).
During FY 2025-26, the Company received five sexual 
harassment complaints, out of which three cases were resolved 
by the ICC and two cases reported in the last quarter of the 
financial year are pending for closure as investigations are in 
progress. No sexual harassment complaint was pending at the 
end of the previous financial year for closure. Further, there 
were no complaints or grievances that remained unresolved 
or pending for a period exceeding ninety days during the 
period under review.Steps taken or impact on 
conservation of energyIn FY 2025-26, 171 energy-saving opportunities were implemented including projects on Heating, 
Ventilation and Air Conditioning (‘HVAC’), Switched-Mode Power Supply (‘SMPS’) and Uninterruptible 
Power Supply (‘UPS’) efficiency enhancement / Optimisation and Consolidation, Smart Lighting 
(conversion of conventional lighting into LED), and Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) enhancement. 
These projects resulted in energy savings of 9.08 million kWh (cumulative) and energy cost savings 
of H8.35 crore.
Steps taken utilising 
alternate sources of energyTata Communications consumed 179 million kWh of energy procured from the national grid during 
FY 2025-26. Almost 76 million units (~42%) out of 179 million units consumed were produced from 
solar and wind energy. This year, we have added 8.91 million units (‘MU’) of Renewable Energy (‘RE’) 
capacity globally. In India, new RE projects were added with varied RE models, with green tariff 
leading to addition of 5.29 MU, Group captive model leading to 3.5 MU of RE addition and Capex based 
Solar roof top leading to addition of 0.12 MU of RE.

 ‘Creating connected societies to advance the wellbeing of 
people and planet.’
 Recognising the 
systemic, global challenges of equitable 
resource distribution, social inequality, environmental 
degradation, and climate change, Tata Communications 
envisions a future that prioritises both social and 
planetary well-being. Through a focused strategy, Tata 
Communications’ CSR programmes aim to advance the 
well-being of people and the planet by emphasizing 
Sustainable Livelihoods and Environmental conservation 
with Education being a key driver for all. This involves 
skill development, entrepreneurship, protection of 
water, biodiversity, and use of renewable energy sources 
to mitigate carbon emissions. We are working towards 
achieving this through collaboration, partnerships, and 
sustainable practices.
  CSR Policy and its alignment with the Tata group 
philosophy:
 CSR at T ata Communications derives inspiration from 
Tata group’s philosophy ‘to improve the quality of life 
of the communities we serve globally through long term 
stakeholder value creation based on leadership with 
trust’. Tata Communications serves to deliver a New World 
of CommunicationsTM which, can and should create social 
value. We are also committed to making a positive, tangible 
impact on the environment and society. Guided by this 
purpose and Tata group’s philosophy, Tata Communications 
leverages its core expertise, partnerships, infrastructure, 
and other resources to facilitate sustainable development 
and create long term shared value for the communities 
we serve, focused primarily on underserved, socially and 
economically backward groups, including, but not limited 
to, women, children, youth, Dalits & Tribals and persons 
with disabilities.
 Complementing 
India’s national priorities and policies 
which reflect the spirit of the UN Sustainable Development 
Goals (‘SDGs’), all efforts at Tata Communications 
are aligned to drive action on the following 11 SDGs in 
accordance with our vision and ambition:
	  SDG 1: End poverty in all its forms everywhere.
	  SDG 3: Ensure healthy lives and promote well-
being for all ages.	  SDG 4: Ensure inclusive and equitable quality 
education and promote lifelong learning 
opportunities for all. 
	  SDG 5: Achieve gender equality and empower all 
women and girls.
	  SDG 7: Ensure access to affordable, reliable, 
sustainable, and modern energy for all.
	  SDG 8: Promote sustained, inclusive, and sustainable 
economic growth, full and productive employment, 
and decent work for all.
	  SDG 10: Reduced Inequality: Reduce inequality 
within and among countries
	  SDG 13: Take urgent action to combat climate 
change and its impacts.
	  SDG 14: Life Below Water: Conserve and sustainably 
use the oceans, seas, and marine resources for 
sustainable development.
	  SDG 15: Life on Land: Protect, restore, and promote 
sustainable use of terrestrial ecosystems, sustainably 
manage forests, combat desertification, and halt and 
reverse land degradation and halt biodiversity loss.
	  SDG 17: Strengthen the means of implementation 
and revitalize the global partnership for 
sustainable development.
 Key focus areas and driv ing principles:
 Tata Communications is committed to conducting its CSR 
activities 
in a manner which is rooted in ethics, promotes 
well-being, and imparts resilience, and supports

with natural environment, Tata Communications identifies

	  Sustainable Livelihoods: Empowering youth, persons

Management Discussion and Analysis
Economic Review
Global Economy1 2
During 2026, the global economy remained steady though uneven, 
with growth stabilising at ~3.1%. This stability has been driven 
largely by sustained demand in services and continued investments 
in digital infrastructure, particularly artificial intelligence ('AI'), 
cloud computing, and high-performance networks. While advanced 
economies experienced relatively slower growth due to tighter 
monetary conditions and elevated interest rates, emerging 
markets continued to be the primary engines of global expansion, 
supported by domestic demand and technology-led trade.
At the same time, underlying risks continue to shape the global 
landscape. Heightened geopolitical tensions, particularly in West 
Asia and other strategic regions, have disrupted energy markets 
and global trade routes. Protectionist policies and evolving tariff 
regimes have added uncertainty to global supply chains, while rising 
public debt and increasing defence spending have contributed to 
fiscal pressures and inflation volatility. These developments have 
reinforced the need for resilient, diversified, and secure global 
infrastructure systems.

Outlook 
Global Economy
The global outlook remains stable but cautious. Growth is expected 
to remain in the range of 3.1%–3.3% over the near term, supported 
by moderating inflation and potential monetary easing in major 
economies. However, risks from geopolitical tensions, commodity 
price volatility, and trade fragmentation continue to pose downside 
challenges. As a result, enterprises globally are increasingly 
prioritising cost optimisation, resilience, and accelerated digital 
transformation to navigate uncertainty.The Indian Economy3 4
India continued to demonstrate strong economic momentum in  
FY 25–26, with GDP growth estimated at 7.4%, positioning it among 
the fastest-growing major economies globally. Growth has been 
broad-based, led by the services sector, which continues to anchor 
economic expansion, alongside resilient domestic consumption and 
sustained public investment in infrastructure.
India’s structural strengths are further reinforced by its rapidly 
expanding digital ecosystem. Widespread internet adoption, 
accelerated 5G rollout, and the scaling of Digital Public 
Infrastructure such as UPI and DigiLocker are transforming 
the economy into a digitally integrated, services-led system. 
Government policy continues to support this shift through 
regulatory reforms, targeted fiscal measures, and incentives for 
digital infrastructure, cloud, and data centre investments.
While the outlook remains favourable, India continues to face 
external risks from global trade uncertainties, commodity price 
volatility, and capital flow fluctuations. Nonetheless, strong 
macroeconomic fundamentals and policy support provide resilience 
against these global headwinds.
Fiscal Policy and Budgetary Measures
India’s fiscal strategy continues to balance growth with 
consolidation, with a strong emphasis on infrastructure-led 
development and digital transformation. The Union Budget 
reinforces this approach through sustained capital expenditure, 
increased allocations for digital infrastructure, artificial 
intelligence, and semiconductor ecosystems, and policy incentives 
for data centres and cloud investments.
Additionally, continued expansion of digital public infrastructure 
and broadband connectivity is enabling greater digital inclusion 
and enterprise adoption, strengthening India’s position as a global 
technology and services hub.
Key Macroeconomic Developments 
Global macroeconomic conditions continue to be shaped by 
geopolitical developments and shifting trade dynamics, particularly 
tensions in West Asia. The escalation of the Iran conflict in early 
2026 has intensified disruptions to key shipping routes, impacting 
energy supply chains, fuel costs, and logistics expenses. These 
developments have contributed to oil price volatility and exposed 
vulnerabilities in globally interconnected trade systems, while 
evolving trade policies and tariff measures have further added 
uncertainty to cross-border trade and supply chain configurations.
This challenging environment, marked by heightened geopolitical 
risks and capital flow volatility, has led to periodic energy price 
spikes and rising freight costs, compressing margins across 
industries. For India, sustained disruptions could affect inflation, 
the current account, and overall economic activity. In this context,

importance of resilient and diversified network infrastructure.
These factors are driving structural shifts in how enterprises 
design supply chains, manage risk, and invest in infrastructure, 
with a growing emphasis on redundancy, diversification, and 
digital integration.
Industry Overview
The Information and Communications Technology ('ICT') sector 
continues to undergo a structural transformation, driven by the 
convergence of connectivity, cloud, and data infrastructure. 
Telecom operators are increasingly evolving from traditional 
connectivity providers to integrated digital solutions partners, 
offering cloud, cybersecurity, IoT , and platform-based services.
AI is at the centre of this transformation, driving new use cases 
across enterprise operations, network management, and customer 
experience. Enterprises are moving beyond pilot programmes 
to large-scale deployments, leading to significant investments 
in data centres, high-performance computing, and AI-enabled 
infrastructure.
This shift is accompanied by the increasing adoption of hybrid 
and multi-cloud environments, the rise of edge computing, and 
the growing importance of secure, low-latency connectivity. As 
digital ecosystems expand, cybersecurity has emerged as a critical 
priority, with organisations investing in advanced protection, 
monitoring, and compliance capabilities.
Global IT Spending Trends5
Global IT spending continues to grow at a strong pace, with total 
spending expected to exceed $6 trillion in 2026, driven largely 
by investments in AI, cloud infrastructure, and enterprise digital 
transformation. Data centre and infrastructure segments are 
witnessing the fastest growth, reflecting the rising demand for 
compute, storage, and high-speed connectivity required to support 
AI workloads and data-intensive applications.
Key Industry Trends
Emergence of AI-Native Networks
AI is rapidly scaling from experimentation to enterprise-wide 
deployment, transforming operations, service delivery, and 
productivity. The ICT ecosystem is evolving towards AI-native 
architectures, embedding intelligence into networks to enable 
real-time optimisation, predictive maintenance, and autonomous 
operations. This shift is also driving demand for high-performance 
computing infrastructure while raising considerations around data 
security, cryptography, and rising infrastructure costs.
Acceleration in Data Consumption and Network Demand
The rapid growth of digital services, video consumption, and 
enterprise applications is significantly increasing global data traffic, 
supported by widespread 5G adoption and device connectivity. In 
India, data usage has already reached high levels, reflecting deep 
digital penetration. This surge is accelerating investments in fiber 
networks, spectrum, and edge infrastructure to ensure scalable 
and cost-efficient capacity expansion.Shift Towards Platform-Based and API-Driven Ecosystems
The ICT industry is transitioning from traditional connectivity 
models to platform-driven ecosystems. Telecom operators are 
leveraging network APIs to enable advanced capabilities such 
as network slicing, location intelligence, and quality-of-service 
integration. This shift is unlocking new monetisation opportunities 
across industries by embedding connectivity into digital services 
and enterprise workflows.
Cloud, Edge and Distributed Computing Convergence
Enterprises are increasingly adopting hybrid and multi-cloud 
strategies, driven by AI adoption, data sovereignty requirements, 
and cost optimisation needs. The convergence of cloud, edge, 
and next-generation networks is enabling low-latency, distributed 
computing and more seamless digital experiences. This evolution 
is reshaping infrastructure design and accelerating demand for 
integrated connectivity solutions.
Enterprise Digitalisation 
Digital transformation continues to accelerate across industries, 
with enterprises adopting cloud, IoT , AI, and platform technologies 
to enhance efficiency and customer experience. In India, rapid 
digital adoption and expanding connectivity infrastructure are 
reinforcing the role of ICT providers as end-to-end transformation 
partners. This trend is driving sustained demand for integrated 
digital and network solutions.
Cybersecurity as a Strategic Imperative
As digital ecosystems expand, cybersecurity has become a 
critical board-level priority. The growing adoption of cloud and 
AI is increasing the complexity of the threat landscape, elevating 
financial and reputational risks. Consequently, organisations are 
investing in advanced security capabilities, real-time monitoring, 
and AI-driven threat detection to strengthen resilience.
Regulatory Evolution
Regulatory frameworks are evolving rapidly in response to data 
privacy, national security, and digital sovereignty concerns. There 
is an increasing focus on data localisation, secure infrastructure, 
and governance of emerging technologies such as AI. At the same 
time, the expansion of digital public infrastructure is driving 
greater compliance requirements and the need for secure, scalable 
digital ecosystems.
Policy developments in India promoting growth in the ICT 
Industry6
India’s policy and regulatory framework continues to be 
a key driver of growth in the ICT sector. The Government 
of India’s approach is centred on expanding digital 
infrastructure, strengthening regulatory clarity, promoting 
indigenous innovation, and enabling technology-led economic 
transformation. These initiatives collectively aim to enhance 
connectivity, deepen digital inclusion, and build a secure and 
globally competitive telecommunications ecosystem.
